connection_type: I have direct personal experience (as an immigrant, refugee, religious minority, or member of a marginalised group)
disclosure_text: I immigrated to Canada 8 years ago
micronarrative: I’ve seen how divided society is over immigration. I’m not against it, but I’ve met families who expect everything to be handed to them—no adjustment, no work.  At first, it’s hard to adjust to foreign language. You need patience to speak slower, to repeat. Some people give up. Others, like me, keep going. I’ve learned that adjusting takes time, but not everyone has the desire to put in the work. In my community, I’ve seen people take advantage of that mindset, leaning on others to fix their problems. It’s frustrating when folks refuse to adapt, expecting resources without reciprocity. Yet I’ve also seen immigrants thrive—slowly, with effort. The town hall scene mirrors this tension: one side demanding enforcement, the other offering tea. I stand somewhere in between, believing hard work pays off, but only if you’re willing to start with the first lesson, the first job, the first attempt to speak a new language.
